text:
devon: heads-up — ran a 10k-run monte carlo over the APAC shared GPU pool for the next 48h. saturation probability >= 0.70 in the baseline config. worried about fragmentation spikes during nightly retrains.

capacitybot: monte-carlo-run finished (run_id=mc-1987). summary: satur_prob=0.73, peak_util=0.94, median_queue_len=8, tail_90_wait=45s.

ana: yikes. is that with current prewarm and soft-affinity on?

devon: yes, include soft-affinity and current prewarm=2 per tenant. no additional reserve.

raj: can you paste the sim config? curious about workload mix — are we assuming full retrain jobs for 2 tenants?

devon: here's the snippet i used:
```bash
capacity-sim --pool apac-shared --horizon 48h --runs 10000 \\  --workload-mix "inference:0.6,train:0.25,batch-tuning:0.15" \\  --prewarm 2 --soft-affinity true --slice-scheduler=adaptive
# result: satur_prob=0.73 peak_util=0.94
```

sophie: ok. two immediate questions: 1) how much does satur_prob drop if we add a 10% short-term reserve? 2) can we tighten eviction budgets to favor interactive?

devon: 10% short-term reserve => satur_prob ~0.48 per quick re-run. tightening eviction budgets (lower host_preempt_quota) helps tail wait for interactive but increases fragmentation: simulations show ~+6% fragmentation metric.

raj: tradeoff then between fragmentation (cost) and SLA risk. we should estimate dollar impact of fragmentation vs penalty of missed SLOs. can someone run a cost-delta per GPU-hour?

mike: i can take cost model. quick ballpark: extra fragmentation overhead ~6% on a 2000 GPU-hour/day fleet ~120 GPU-hours/day wasted. at $2.5/hr that is ~$300/day. missed SLA from satur events (if we had to divert to higher-cost dedicated cloud) could be multiple thousands.

ana: good data. proposal: 1) enable a temporary 10% bubble reserve for next 72h; 2) set interactive eviction_budget to 0.02 (was 0.05) for canary tenants; 3) schedule big retrains to off-peak APAC windows and advertise to teams.

raj: +1 for bubble reserve. need ops runbook for rollback if we suddenly lose capacity in EU region or have a hardware failure.

devon: adding runbook note: if reserve causes underutilization in US/EU, we run cross-region burstbackfill by marking low-prio jobs with region=any for next 24h. fallback: auto-scale dedicated pool by 5 cards if satur_prob > 0.8.

capacitybot: action created: /tickets/INFRA-4821 "APAC bubble reserve + eviction budget canary" assigned -> mike, devon. due 24h.

mike: will compute cost-delta and post in thread in 2h. also can we patch slice-scheduler to emit a "saturation_signal" metric so auto-scaling can trigger earlier?

devon: yes, i can add a hotfix that emits satur_prob estimate every hour using the fast sim. will throttle to avoid noise.

ana: reminder -> tell platform teams to add a short note in the console when reserve is active so tenant owners know we may throttle batch jobs for 72h.

sophie: sounds good. quick check: any networking constraints at peak that would worsen queueing? last time we saw pod-to-pod transfer bandwidth became a bottleneck during large checkpoint copies.

devon: good point. sim didn't model network spikes. but ops reported one transient during last Saturday (packet drops on nap-az3). i've added a manual check to verify heartbeat loss <0.1% before enabling reserve; if >0.1% we hold.

raj: thanks. i'm updating capacity forecast doc with these mitigations. i'll flag for oncall to watch the satur_prob metric today.

mike: posted cost delta: extra $360/day for 10% reserve vs estimated risk of $3k+ outage cost. recommend proceeding.

ana: ok team — proceeding with reserve now, canary eviction changes for tenant group A only. watch alerts. :thumbsup:

sophie: ack. i'll message impacted tenants and update the console banner.

devon: rolling the hotfix in 5m to emit hourly satur_prob. will update when live.

capacitybot: ticket INFRA-4821 updated: status=In Progress, hotfix_deploy=1987654412."
